name: manual_3e5b1a
claim: Judge a LAN send in two steps. Direct-drop success is the drop's own JSON: ok true, a received_at and a byte count equal to the file size; that proves the receiving front end accepted that many bytes, not that the content is identical. For a reciprocal claim of delivery, require a verified peer CA on the channel and a receiver receipt whose hash, recomputed by the receiver from its stored bytes (LF-normalised when text may have been line-ending translated), equals the sender's hash. A queued record is not delivery, and a count of queued sidecars counts files, not peers: read the per-item sidecar before stating how many peers a send reached.

decisions.notes: Accepted per review of PT PR 492: byte counts show the front end accepted bytes, not identical content; reciprocal delivery needs a verified peer CA and a receiver receipt hash recomputed from stored bytes. Supersedes the earlier delivery-evidence lesson while keeping its drop-JSON and sidecar guidance.
